raw_text:
Independent review of run r-20260929T123941126119-llac-worker-slots-publish-consistently at head e41ea962 against base c3207114, the section-21 repair that makes the published worker_slots follow from the published requests_per_run and pins the window clip and the unreadable-header branch with tests. imas_ambix/agent/router.py:354 rounds the ratio once and derives the slot count from that published figure, and a ratio that rounds to zero is withheld together with the slots its arithmetic would divide. The three new tests are the preceding review's own findings turned into fixtures: three runs at 720.009 busy seconds, a request opened 100 s before the window and released 50 s inside it, and an over-long run-id header driven through the real request path. The repeated docstring phrase is corrected and the node's fragment ends with a newline. The repair lands what it was dispatched for, and one branch it introduces is reached by no test.

Goal fidelity. Section 21's deploy acceptance is that the published worker_slots equals the formula applied to the document's own width, requests_per_run and live_runs. Before this run the ledger published round(ratio, 3) and divided by the unrounded ratio, so the identity could fail; router.py:354-372 now rounds once and derives the count from the rounded figure, so the identity holds by construction. Driven directly rather than through the node's tests, the ledger at head publishes ratio 0.8 with 17 slots on the dispatcher's own fixture and computes the same 17 from those published figures, where the base revision publishes the same 0.8 beside 16 (review-ledger-probe.log). The node also adds a guard the plan does not describe: a ratio that rounds to 0.000 withholds both derived fields. That branch is defensible -- at base the same regime publishes ratio 0.0 beside 35997 slots, on which the plan's own formula divides by zero -- but it is a third null condition that section 21's definitions, which name only fewer than three live runs and under 300 s of history, do not carry.

Independent verification. Four arms were run by this review under the shared project interpreter, each log header naming the revision, the tree, the module under test as imported and the resolved working directory. Head arm at e41ea962 inside the reviewed worktree, the tree's only copy: the node's declared four-file gate, 39 passed, exit 0 (review-head-gate.log); the serving-interpreter parse check 1 passed; ruff check imas_ambix tests printed all checks passed. Base arm at c3207114 in a scratch copy at /tmp/rev-llac-publish/base: the same four files, 36 passed, exit 0 (review-base-gate.log), so the run adds no failing test by id or by count. The base revision's router.py with the head test files kept fails exactly the two tests that assert the published identity (review-base-router-head-tests.log), which is the previously recorded defect reproducing where it was recorded. The head tree with the window clip removed fails exactly the new clip test (review-no-clip-probe.log), so the guard the preceding review found unpinned now fires. The reviewed run's own two negative-control logs were read: the clip log's first line repeats its declared mutation verbatim and ends 1 failed with EXIT=1, the unrounded-ratio log ends assert 16 == 17 with EXIT=1, and neither repeats the preceding run's trap of a red arm whose last line reads EXIT=0. The reviewed worktree was not modified: git status was empty before and after every arm.
